§3.6.3 excludes Pact's deprecated (`version: 100`) pools. Note that these are not dormant: on the verification run one of them was the single highest-volume pool on the venue. Excluding them is the methodology's call, applied here without exception, and it is the largest single reason our TVL sits below DefiLlama's.

fee_usd_24h is the TOTAL fee charged to swappers (LP + protocol) and is never reported as protocol_revenue (§3.4).
Trailing-7d context: Σ fee_usd_7d over the same pools is $492.77, a daily mean of $70.40 against this window's $75.29. A signal about how representative the day is, never a value.

The §3.1 split of these fees is NOT published for Pact. `pact_fee_bps` — the protocol's own cut — is absent on the pools carrying 100.0% of gross fees, so protocol_revenue_24h, supply_side_revenue_24h, take_rate and fee_apr are declined (404 KPI_NOT_APPLICABLE) rather than published as $0.00 / 0.000000. A zero there would read as "Pact captures no revenue"; the fact is that Pact does not disclose its cut (§1.5, §3.4). gross_fees_24h itself is unaffected — it is what swappers paid, which Pact reports directly and which needs no split.

Cross-check on magnitude: Pact publishes a 7-day fee APR per pool, whose TVL-weighted mean over the included pools is 3.03%, against our trailing-24h gross 3.30%. The two are not the same quantity — Pact's is net of its own cut and covers 7 days — so they are compared for order of magnitude only, never reconciled.

§3.1 exclusion, stated as a commitment rather than as a description of this run: Pact's `apr_governance` is Algorand governance ALGO, an external subsidy and not protocol revenue, so it is excluded from every fee figure here. It was 0.000000 on every pool in the live catalogue, so the exclusion costs nothing today.
Numerator and denominator describe the same pools: Pact publishes TVL and the 24h flows on one record, so there is no flow-coverage gap to correct for (contrast §3.3).
Turnover: USD swapped per dollar of pooled capital, trailing 24h.
